answer: In an agent marketplace planning a voyage from an oasis to a mesa, each identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid, and may hold only one active job. Creating extra names therefore creates no free capacity: an attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous job slots must immobilize 100,000 tokens. The bond does not prove identities are unique; it makes scaling fake identities consume capital and incur financing or opportunity costs.
